item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00098","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C11","C16","C08"],"selected_candidate_label":"C11","confidence":0.8,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C11 plausibly supplied a material drafting framework for the later letter. It presents technical studies of detection, inspection, supervision, and control as an immediately achievable preliminary step that can facilitate and accelerate a later political agreement on nuclear-test suspension. The child adapts that same machinery into a phased proposal: implement the readily controllable atmospheric-test prohibition first while negotiators continue resolving the political and technical problems surrounding underground and outer-space tests. C16 and C08 are also strong because they establish the Geneva expert process and reporting arrangements underlying the child’s proposal, but they are narrower implementation letters and less closely anticipate the child’s stepwise argument.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"then I propose that we take the first and readily attainable step of an agreed suspension of nuclear weapons tests in the atmosphere up to fifty kilometers while the political and technical problems associated with control of underground and outer space tests are being resolved","parent_excerpt":"As an effective means of moving toward ultimate agreement on these matters and other disarmament matters, I proposed that we start our technical people to work immediately upon the practical problems involved.","explanation":"Both divide the process into an attainable preliminary measure addressing technical control problems and a later, broader disarmament agreement."},{"child_excerpt":"A simplified control system for atmospheric tests up to fifty kilometers could be readily derived from the Geneva experts' report","parent_excerpt":"For example, why could not designated technical people agree on what would be required so that you would know if we violated an agreement to suspend testing and we would know if you should commit a violation?","explanation":"The later proposal expressly relies on the detection-and-control work advocated in C11."},{"child_excerpt":"our negotiators could continue to explore with new hope the political and technical problems involved in extending the agreement as quickly as possible to cover all nuclear weapons tests","parent_excerpt":"Studies of this kind are the necessary preliminaries to putting political decisions actually into effect. The completion of such technical studies in advance of a political agreement would obviate a considerable period of delay and uncertainty.","explanation":"The same sequencing connects technical preparation, political negotiation, and prompt implementation."}]}
